children: Nike
has had a rough year so far, with shares down 46% year-to-date as it contends with a myriad of issues, including increased competition and shifting consumer tastes.
We asked Seeking Alpha analysts
and
how they thought the iconic company could get back on track.
: Nike

is already doing some things right. For example, plans to overhaul the supply chain and boost efficiency should help with the turnaround. However, the largest problem that the company faces is a lack of consumer demand and enthusiasm.

Over the years, the brand has used political/social justice ad campaigns significantly. This has resulted in the alienation of many consumers, particularly in the U.S., who hold different views on these topics. Their history of engagement in polarizing marketing seems to have taken a toll.

The company is already shifting their ad strategy as they plan to reposition Sportswear and their Jordan brand. However, I believe they should heavily double down on getting back to their roots and celebrating athletic excellence in sports. This should make Nike resonate with many more consumers and address the fundamental issue that is weighing on their sales.
While it is impossible to change brand perception overnight, this is the best move that they can make to start getting their business back on track, in my view.
Luca Socci: Nike

faces a demand problem, which is consistent with the fact that the company belongs to the fashion industry, where consumer tastes and preferences can swing quickly. A business can’t run only on correctly predicting demand; it also needs to be able to depend less on the cyclicality of trends.
In part, Nike
has already achieved this status. It has been around for decades while we have seen the rise and fall of many smaller brands. But I think Nike
has to focus on performance so that at least some of its products are considered the highest-quality option.

This could be the model for each price tier, which would allow Nike to charge a premium while also making it clear that it offers customers the best athletic experience possible. Lifestyle franchises should not be as important as they became after the pandemic. While logistics savings can surely help, Nike
needs to focus on what revitalizes its revenues.
